title: Closer relatives tend to be closer together in time and space

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Closer relatives tend to be closer together in time and space

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Because forms within each class are connected by ordinary generation, the more closely two forms are related by descent, the nearer they will generally be to each other in time and in geographic space.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: and the more nearly any two forms are related in blood, the nearer they will generally stand to each other in time and space;

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter XII, “Geographical Distribution, continued”; section “Summary”. Scope: all organisms, living and fossil

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch12-18: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.80

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: All principal quantities have standard definitions and public data. A broad multi-clade analysis is feasible, though the fossil record makes full-scope estimates biased.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For pairs of living and fossil taxa, regress geographic and temporal separation on phylogenetic distance while accounting for sampling and clade. A general increase in separation with evolutionary distance supports the prediction.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Spatial autocorrelation and uneven fossil sampling can create the pattern.

Fossil placements and ages are uncertain.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Phylogenetic, geographic and temporal distances are ordinary variables, and a positive partial association is an obvious confirming result for a claim qualified by 'generally'. Public trees, occurrences and fossil occurrences cover enough clades to accept or reject that general tendency, even though most fossil species lack a resolved phylogeny. Sampling bias is serious and is the reason discriminating power is not higher.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Across living and fossil species, test whether phylogenetic distance increases with geographic distance and with separation in time, using divergence dates or stratigraphic midpoints. The claim is confirmed if both partial associations are positive across large clades, and refuted if close relatives are no nearer in space or time than distant relatives once sampling effort is controlled.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Fossil finds are concentrated in well-worked basins, so apparent closeness in time and space partly tracks rock exposure.

Geography has historically influenced which specimens taxonomists treat as separate species, which can tighten the spatial pattern by construction.

Molecular divergence dates are model-based proxies for the temporal nearness Darwin described from fossils and living ranges.

fields.label: Hypothesis
fields.value: If closer relatives are generally nearer in space and time, then (space, living forms) phylogenetic distance between bird species should correlate positively with the geographic distance between their range centroids, with congeneric pairs closer than confamilial pairs and those closer than pairs from different families of the same order; and (time, fossil forms) genera in the same family should have first appearances closer in geological time than genera in different families of the same order.

fields.label: Method
fields.value: Space: 5883 bird species with a one-to-one BirdLife-BirdTree name match, a tree tip and an AVONET range centroid. Patristic distances were computed on the MCC tree; 1999655 random species pairs were drawn and the Spearman correlation between patristic and great-circle centroid distance was compared with 99 permutations of centroids among species; medians of centroid distance were tabulated for congeneric, confamilial and same-order pairs. Time: PBDB accepted genera with family, order and first-appearance ages; within each order, genus pairs (all pairs, or 500000 random pairs for very large orders) were split into same-family and different-family, and the difference of medians of |dFAD| was compared with 99 permutations of family labels within orders.

fields.label: Pass criterion
fields.value: Space (all extant birds with a range centroid in AVONET and a tip in the BirdTree Hackett MCC tree supplied with AVONET): (S1) the Spearman correlation between patristic distance and great-circle centroid distance across a fixed random sample of 2,000,000 species pairs is positive, and exceeds all of 99 permutations in which centroids are shuffled among species (p <= 0.01); (S2) median centroid distance is strictly ordered congeneric pairs < confamilial non-congeneric pairs < same-order different-family pairs. Time (Paleobiology Database genera of Mammalia and of Mollusca with first-appearance ages and family/order assignments): (T1) in each of the two groups, the median absolute difference in first-appearance midpoint age between pairs of genera in the same family is smaller than between pairs of genera in different families of the same order, and this difference exceeds all of 99 permutations of family labels within orders (p <= 0.01). The space clause passes if S1 and S2 hold; the time clause passes if T1 holds in both groups. Verdict 'supports' if both clauses pass, 'mixed' if one passes, 'refutes' if neither.

fields.label: Fail criterion
fields.value: The space clause fails if the Spearman correlation is <= 0 or does not exceed the permutation distribution at p <= 0.01, or if the median distances are not strictly ordered by relatedness. The time clause fails if in either group same-family genus pairs are not closer in first-appearance time than different-family same-order pairs, or the difference is not significant at p <= 0.01 against the within-order permutation null. Both failing refutes the claim.

fields.label: Unit
fields.value: Spearman rho between patristic distance and centroid great-circle distance, bird species pairs

fields.label: Uncertainty
fields.value: permutation p = 0.010; permuted rho range -0.0071 to 0.0068

fields.label: Interpretation
fields.value: 'Related by descent' is measured for living birds as patristic distance on a dated molecular supertree (Jetz et al. 2012 BirdTree, Hackett backbone MCC tree as distributed with AVONET), a modern reinterpretation of Darwin's classification-based relatedness, and for fossils by shared family versus shared order in PBDB taxonomy, which is closer to Darwin's own usage. 'Nearer in geographic space' is the great-circle distance between AVONET breeding-range centroids. 'Nearer in time' is the absolute difference between first-appearance ages (midpoints of PBDB first-appearance age ranges) of genera. Only two living/fossil systems are tested, not 'all organisms'; birds are chosen because tree, taxonomy and centroids come from a single curated source, and mammals and molluscs because they are the best-sampled terrestrial and marine fossil records. Sampling and taxonomic-practice confounds (geography informing species limits; fossils concentrated in a few basins) are noted as caveats rather than corrected.

fields.label: Datasets
fields.value:
AVONET ELEData.zip: TraitData/AVONET1_BirdLife.csv (range centroids, taxonomy), PhylogeneticData/HackettStage1_0001_1000_MCCTreeTargetHeights.nex (BirdTree Hackett MCC tree, 6670 species) and BirdLife-BirdTree crosswalk.csv

Paleobiology Database taxa lists (genus rank) with first/last appearance ages and classification for Mammalia and Mollusca

fields.label: Caveats
fields.value:
The overall Spearman correlation between patristic and geographic distance is small (about 0.03) although far outside the permutation null; the relationship is concentrated at shallow phylogenetic depth (congeneric and confamilial pairs) and saturates at the order level, where median centroid distance is no smaller within than between orders.

Pooled permutation nulls for the fossil clause are not centred on zero because orders differ in family structure and age spread; the observed differences are judged against that null, not against zero.

Space is tested in one class (birds) and time in two fossil groups at genus level; the claim is stated for all organisms, living and fossil.

Range centroids collapse each species to a point; sister species with adjacent but large ranges can appear far apart, which weakens rather than inflates the correlation.

Species limits in birds have historically been drawn partly on geography (allopatric forms), which can tighten the congeneric-pair pattern by construction.

Fossil first appearances are truncated by sampling and concentrated in well-sampled basins and intervals; genera in the same family are often described from the same formations, which can make same-family FADs look closer than they are.

Family and order assignments in PBDB are of uneven quality, especially for Mollusca; genera with unassigned family or order were dropped.

Patristic distance on the BirdTree MCC tree is a model-based divergence estimate, a modern proxy for Darwin's relatedness by descent.
